coordinates.locator: OSM geometry of the Mont Blanc Tunnel; mid-length point (see note)
coordinates.note: Midpoint along the OpenStreetMap-traced centreline of the 11.49 km tunnel (ways 4525912 + 205544546), computed by cumulative great-circle length. The NUSEX paper says only that the experiment 'is situated half way along the road tunnel'; the exact cave (an INFN garage) is not given, and a tunnel trace is not a survey. Campus-grade point, not a detector position.
coordinates.quote: is situated half way along the road tunnel under Mont Blanc linking France and Italy

depth_mwe.note: The Monopole '83 chapter gives 'approximately 5000 m.w.e.'; the 1985 ICRC paper gives a minimum overburden of about 5000 hg/cm^2 (= 5000 m.w.e.).
depth_mwe.quote: is at a depth of approximately 5000 m.w.e.

name: Mont Blanc Tunnel laboratory (NUSEX cave)
notes: The tunnel crosses the French-Italian border. In the OpenStreetMap trace the French way is 7.53 km long and the midpoint of the whole tunnel lies 5.75 km from the French portal, so the point falls in the French section and the site is filed under France; no source locates the NUSEX cave itself, so the country is an inference from the midpoint.

place.region: Mont Blanc Tunnel (France-Italy border, between Chamonix and Courmayeur)

summary.plain: A cave beside the Mont Blanc road tunnel, roughly half way between France and Italy and under about five thousand metres of water-equivalent rock, where the NUSEX detector ran from 1982.
summary.technical: Underground cave off the Mont Blanc road tunnel, mid-length, at about 5000 m.w.e. Marked with an approximate point at the middle of the traced tunnel.
